items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: Zutty's uncle, a fellow played the banjo called Willie Bontemps -- and he's a very nice man -- ... Willie put his arms around me. He said, 'Don't worry, son, I'll take care of you.'

ctx.x: this Willie Santiago. He was the banjo player in New Orleans. You know, he used to come in at night and he'd sleep. He'd tune up his banjo and he'd go to sleep all night. Time to knock off or get off -- it was about ten to 15 minutes before we would knock off, he'd stretch himself and say, "Oh, boy, I feel good." And everybody in the band would say, "You should feel good. You slept all night."

And we'd go out and they had a club and everybody's turn -- whoever's turn it was -- they had to fill, they had what they call in those days a "cooler." They put ice in there and they'd fill it with wine and they had to cook the dinner for the club. And it was Willie's turn that night, that day, in fact, it was a Friday. So he went out and he bought a big fish, a big red snapper, filled the cooler full of wine, and he went out and got the fish when the market opened early in the morning, six o'clock. And he got…
So then from then -- Then, getting back to New York, one night I went to work with Luis Russell at a place called The Nest Club, and I worked with Luis Russell for a long time.
